name: OCTAVIA E. BUTLER LANDING SITE
brief: Touchdown location of the Mars 2020 Perseverance rover on Sol 0 (February 18, 2021). Comprises a flat, fractured basaltic lava or impact-melt sheet blanketed with a thin veneer of aeolian sand.

soil_regolith.grain_size: Fine to medium sand (150–350 µm) with basalt pebble armor
soil_regolith.soil_bearing_capacity: 160 kPa (High firmness / Nominal rover wheel traction)

name: KODIAK BUTTE
brief: Prominent flat-topped erosional butte south of the main delta front. Mastcam-Z and SuperCam long-distance imaging revealed distinct steeply dipping deltaic foreset beds (15°–20°), confirming a sustained ancient paleolake highstand.

soil_regolith.grain_size: Silt to fine sand (<63 µm to 125 µm); rounded boulder topsets
soil_regolith.soil_bearing_capacity: 140 kPa (Moderately firm talus / slope slip risk on scarp)

name: THREE FORKS SAMPLE DEPOT
brief: Historic surface cache depot for the NASA-ESA Mars Sample Return (MSR) campaign. Perseverance deposited 10 titanium sample tubes on the flat ground here between Dec 2022 and Jan 2023 as an operational backup.

brief: Navajo for "amidst the sand". A geologically unique layered ultramafic unit featuring heavy aeolian sand ripples and cumulate igneous rocks that crystallized deep inside a magma chamber before water filled the crater.

brief: Steep exposure of fine-grained deltaic mudstones deposited during a quiescent phase of Lake Jezero. Abrasion patch "Swift Run" revealed intense sulfate mineral concentrations and the highest biosignature preservation potential discovered to date.

soil_regolith.grain_size: Ultra-fine clay/silt (<10 µm) with crystalline sulfate veins
